status: REGISTERED 2026-11-16, before any timed run. Repeats, primary GPU and the fixed W1024/256 setting were agreed with the team on 2026-11-16. A timed run is valid only from a commit that contains this file unchanged.
recording: not recorded by the team's ledger runner (not in the repository); self-recorded manifests plus one gate receipt per driver process (code/gated_run.py)
queries: 500 calibration queries only, file order; held-out untouched
fixed: range_scores kernel body (variant 5), index format, scoring, selection, merge; range size 1024 positions, 256 threads

implementations.sequential: control: one query at a time, each on its own slot and stream
implementations.streams: all queries of a batch launched before any is collected, one stream per query
implementations.batched: one launch per batch, grid (ranges, batch), last block detected per query

later: full collection (8,841,823 passages) with the shared prepared inputs pinned in experiments/2026-11-15-full-collection-baselines/configs/protocol.json (GSP e838dfbf..., W1024 RBP c7669620..., oracle 7a63bb52...), never an independent rebuild; a registration entry with batch sizes that fit the modelled memory is added before those runs. The 1M run is a labelled scaling study.

correctness_gate.where: inside code/run_timing.sh, with the same binary, source commit and GPU as the timed processes; timing does not start unless every check passes
correctness_gate.edge_cases: tests/check_range_batch.py: synthetic fixtures (single document, empty documents, ties across ranges, partial last range, 128-term queries, repeated terms, empty index, empty and no-posting queries), all three modes, batch 1, a partial last batch, a batch equal to and larger than the query file; 1 warm-up + 2 rounds, VERIFY=1 (poisoned buffers, counter read-back, in-driver CPU reference) and independent Python rankings
correctness_gate.runtime_gate: every driver process reports its resolved configuration and behaviour marks before computing; code/gated_run.py compares them with an independently derived expectation (reviewed parser experiments/2026-11-15-range-worker-sweep/code/expected.py) and releases or rejects the process. Marks distinguish sequential, streams and batched execution.
correctness_gate.runtime_rejections: three deliberate mismatches (execution mode, batch size, score threads) must each be rejected before any result file exists
correctness_gate.real_data: every timed configuration plus batch 7 (partial last batch) per mode and k: 500 calibration queries, 1 warm-up + 1 round, VERIFY=2 (poisoned buffers, counter read-back), every answer compared with the CPU oracle file
correctness_gate.earlier_runs: 20261115-cuda2-iso-01 and 20261115-cuda2-batched-01 (code/check_isolation.sh, code/check_batched.sh) are correctness records for earlier commits on RTX 2080 Ti; they do not replace the checks above
correctness_gate.rule: any mismatch, rejection failure or driver failure stops the run before timing; it is preserved and reported, not rerun unchanged

timing.order: rotating across the three processes: in process p configuration (i + offset_p) mod n runs i-th, offsets 0, ceil(n/3), ceil(2n/3)
timing.batch_formation: consecutive queries in file order; the last batch may be partial; batches are complete before timing starts, so no wait-to-form time is included or modelled
timing.boundary: per batch, wall clock: host build of query arguments, query transfer (kernel argument for sequential/streams, one H2D copy for batched), all kernels, top-k D2H to pinned memory, event completion. Excluded: index load/upload, tie-rank and buffer setup, runtime gate, file output, correctness checking. Device event spans are diagnostics only.
timing.gpu_check: before each process: no other compute process on the target GPU (poll 60 s, abort after 60 min). During each process: one nvidia-smi sample per second of the processes on the target GPU. A timing process during which another process was sampled, or whose sampler failed, is ineligible: it is kept under raw/ineligible/ and replaced, at most 3 replacements per run. No sampled foreign process is not proof of an exclusive GPU.
timing.correctness_during_timing: every saved top-k of every timing process compared with the CPU oracle
timing.cpu: driver pinned to CPU 0; gate and sampler pinned to CPU 1
timing.identity: source commit, binary SHA-256 and GPU UUID in every receipt; index and query SHA-256 in the manifest; the analysis refuses mixed identities
timing.raw_answers: ranked answers of every correctness and timing process kept losslessly: each distinct per-round answer body stored once (gzip, named by SHA-256) and a per-process receipt that rebuilds the full listing to its original SHA-256 (code/pack_answers.py)
timing.valid_results: a completed valid result is not rerun to obtain better numbers; technical failures are preserved, reviewed and repaired in a fresh run directory

metrics.throughput_qps: queries / sum of batch_wall_ms over a measured round, per process; reported per configuration as the median over rounds and processes with the range
metrics.completion_latency_ms: per query, from batch start to that query's results on the host; reported as median, p95 and p99 over queries, per configuration
metrics.batch_processing_ms: batch_wall_ms per full batch; partial batches reported separately

memory.tracked_allocation_bytes: device buffers the driver allocates itself: shared index + per-query bytes x batch; checked against the independent expectation at the gate; excludes the CUDA context and allocator rounding
memory.device_used_delta_bytes: change in device used memory across the driver's allocations, read once by the driver
memory.sampled_process_memory_mib: largest one-second nvidia-smi sample of the driver process; a sampled maximum, not an exact peak
memory.rule: reported separately from each other and from time; never mixed or called peak without the qualifier

contrasts: streams / sequential and batched / sequential throughput at each batch size and k
batched / streams throughput at each batch size and k
each mode at batch b / the same mode at batch 1
analysis: paired by measured round and process; geometric mean of throughput ratios; 10,000-draw crossed bootstrap over rounds and processes, seed 20261117, conditional on the calibration set and session; completion-latency percentiles are descriptive, not serving tails

hardware.primary: RTX 4070 on cuda5, UUID GPU-ab7b89ba-5664-fd05-e352-a4bc034e5ff7, sm_89 (the GPU of the full-collection baseline). Shared machine: runs are announced to the team first; no exclusive slot is implied.
hardware.replication: RTX 2080 Ti on cuda2, sm_75, same protocol, reported as a separately labelled replication; the GPU UUID is recorded in the run
hardware.fixed_setting: range size 1024 positions, 256 threads on both; no per-GPU tuning in this registration
hardware.rule: results from different GPU models are never pooled

not_in_this_registration: held-out queries, arrival processes or batch-formation wait, multi-GPU, changes to scoring/selection/storage, pruning
parent_results: Full-collection single-query baseline: experiments/2026-11-15-full-collection-baselines (measured source f10c7e7). Its numbers are not re-measured or extended here.
limits: 128-term query limit of the scorer; calibration queries have at most 95 terms; held-out lengths are not audited here
guarded uint32 accumulation equals uint64 only on the verified integer domain (see the full-collection report); arithmetic labels are kept
completion is stamped by polling events on one host thread; batches are formed before timing, so no arrival process or formation wait
three processes on a shared GPU; intervals are conditional on this session
comparisons are among our own three execution modes on the same scorer; no claim about released GPUSparse or CPU BMP
